report_name: Bipartisan 'Quantum-GUARD Act' Introduced to Protect US Electric Grid

vulnerabilities.name: Vulnerability of Public-Key Cryptography to Quantum Attacks
vulnerabilities.description: Current public-key cryptography standards used in the U.S. electric grid are vulnerable to being broken by future fault-tolerant quantum computers, which could allow adversaries to decrypt sensitive energy sector communications and manipulate grid operations.

identities.name: U.S. Senate
identities.description: A bipartisan group of U.S. Senators introduced the Quantum Grid Utility Assurance and Resilient Defense (Quantum-GUARD) Act of 2026 to proactively address threats from quantum computing to the U.S. electric grid.

identities.name: Department of Energy
identities.description: Directed by the Quantum-GUARD Act to study cybersecurity risks from quantum computing to the electric sector and to establish a testing environment for post-quantum cryptography (PQC).

identities.name: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission
identities.description: Required by the Quantum-GUARD Act to initiate a rulemaking process to incorporate quantum-related risks into its mandatory reliability standards for the U.S. bulk-power system.

identities.name: National Institute of Standards and Technology
identities.description: Finalized post-quantum cryptography (PQC) standards in 2024, which prompted the legislative action of the Quantum-GUARD Act.

identities.name: U.S. bulk-power system
identities.description: The critical infrastructure sector that the Quantum-GUARD Act of 2026 aims to protect from future cybersecurity threats posed by quantum computers.

relationships.source_name: National Institute of Standards and Technology
